 Baton Rouge food groups expand Thanksgiving distributions 
 Greater Baton Rouge Food Bank and Catholic Charities describe holiday food programs and ways to donate 
 Watch 9News at 6 weekdays with Greg Meriwether, plus Meteorologist Dr. Steve Caparotta, and Sports Director Jacques Doucet By Georgia Peck Published : Nov. 19, 2026 at 5:50 PM CST | Updated : 46 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google BATON ROUGE, La. (WAFB) - The Greater Baton Rouge Food Bank and Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Baton Rouge are distributing food ahead of Thanksgiving, and both organizations are asking the public for donations.
 Brian Hightower, chief development officer and general counsel for the food bank, said needs increase around Thanksgiving and the holidays.
 “We do find that around Thanksgiving time and the holidays time towards the end of the year that need increases,” Hightower said. “This year, obviously, costs are up, and holidays in and of themselves bring about a desire to be with family and to enjoy a shared meal.”
 Food bank holiday box distributions
 Hightower said corporate sponsors pay for boxes of food that are given out at holiday distributions. He named Nutrien, CF Industries, and Exxon as sponsors.
 “Companies like Nutrien, CF Industries, Exxon, companies like that, support us by donating money to buy boxes of food for holiday box programs,” Hightower said. “And so we’ll go out and serve alongside those corporations and those partners and distribute food to neighbors in need.”
 Hightower said the food bank has held distributions this week and has more scheduled at the end of the week, over the weekend and into next week. He said the boxes are meant to replicate a typical holiday meal and can include canned goods, boxed stuffing, and proteins.
 On average, the food bank serves 45,000 to 49,000 people a month through 145 partner agencies, Hightower said. That figure also includes programs such as senior box, after-school, and backpack programs. He said sponsored holiday distributions add about 5,000 boxes over the next two months.
 Hightower said people can find out about the distributions through the food bank’s social media channels.
 How to donate to the food bank
 Hightower said people can donate at brfoodbank.org with a one-time gift or sign up for Nourish 365, the food bank’s monthly recurring gift program. People can also host a food drive or drop off food in bins at partner grocery stores and retail locations.
 “This time of year, money to the Greater Baton Rouge Food Bank and food donated to food bank really makes a difference,” Hightower said.
 Catholic Charities food programs
 Stephanie Sterling, executive director of Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Baton Rouge, said the organization distributes food boxes in Baton Rouge, Albany, Donaldsonville, Morganza, and Convent.
 Sterling said Catholic Charities also runs a retail rescue program with Sam’s Club and Walmart stores. Staff pick up close-dated food several times a week, she said. The food is distributed to community members and to about eight partner agencies.
 Sterling said Catholic Charities distributed more than 300,000 pounds of retail rescue food last year, worth more than $700,000.
 “We know in Louisiana, we are number one for senior hunger and number two in childhood hunger,” Sterling said.
 Sterling said the organization serves about 2,000 families every month throughout the year. She said it distributes food every month and to community partners every day of the week. Its mobile distribution runs on a different day each month, including during November, she said.
 Catholic Charities works with the Greater Baton Rouge Food Bank for USDA food and retail rescue food, Sterling said.
 Internal collection and online donations
 This Thanksgiving, employees at Catholic Charities and the Catholic Life Center are collecting food for the organization’s food program. Sterling said the collection is internal and is not open to public drop-off.
 Sterling said the public can donate online at catholiccharitiesbr.org to the food program or to the greatest need in the community. She said the food program has costs that include fuel, boxes, truck maintenance, and refrigeration and freezers.
